english: Doviello Berserkers carry crude weapons into battle, a throwing rock bigger than a man's head or a stout branch. They use these makeshift weapons because they are temporary. The first opponent killed became the weapon of choice. Grabbed by the ankles they would be swung like a meaty flail. Blood sprayed over opponents and every swing would lose more and more of the corpse until another was needed to replace the first. At this point in the battle the "weapons" were always readily available. Occasionally an opponent would be grabbed while still alive. The effect of being beaten by a bloody body that was screaming at you while it happened is traumatizing to even the most hardened warrior. Few armies were willing to face them. -from "Pack of Wolves" by Dentaro
Thalatth the Scaled Dragon
Commander

[TAB]The Gentle One. The Guardian of the Placid Sea. The Scarecrow of the Coward God. The Neutered-Guard-Dog of the Deep. These are translations of some of the more respectful titles recorded in the Dabrei Tanninim (a hundred scroll chronicle of the Godswar composed three decades before Kylorin's birth, known only from commentaries recovered from the Library fo Barathrum) to refer to a beast whose true name had already been forgotten. [PARAGRAPH:2]While gods and dragons warred across Creation, this creature lay safe at the feet of Danalin, below his throne, guarding against threats to Maenalus that never came. He had been made as a sign (an empty threat, some claimed) that Danalin would defend his beloved Aifons if their armies were ever to encroach upon his sacred waters The Great Scaled Dragon was one of many beasts made for this purpose, but his presence was more imposing than all the rest of his lord's horde. [PARAGRAPH:2]Danalin and Sucellus were not dragged into the Godswar until it neared an end; their armies of beasts, angels, and elementals saw little action. The Great Scaled Dragon fought only 4 days in the war before the great truce. He never turned the tide of a single battle in that age, and rarely dared to lead any assault in person. His greatest claim to fame was that he was the first beast to retreat for the meeting at the Seven Pines, and was the first to leave Erebus after the signing of the Compact. The Aifons once sang praises of his prudence. Men and Elves mocked the monster's cowardice. In Kylorin's early armies, "Scaled Dragon" became the byword for a paper tiger. That would change. [PARAGRAPH:2]Incomprehensible omens, visions, dreams of torment too horrid to describe, and prophecies that left the seers catatonic became almost commonplace during the Patrian Civil War. Many signs pointed to a catastrophe looming over the Aifons, and some even named the date of their demise, but no one knew that threat they faced. Kylorin's former pupil, the Aifon Trenton Majosi, traveled all the lands of Erebus seeking salvation for his people, but found none. The closest he came was uncovering a ritual he was told could summon his god into Erebus itself, to personally protect them from whatever doom awaited them. [PARAGRAPH:2]Midway through performing the ritual, perhaps mesmerized by the pendulum swing of his spear, his mind began to wander, pondering the fate of the friends he had made on his quest. Tears welled up within him. As his chants approached the final stanza, he choked up and fell to his knees, unable to continue. He had realized that his actions would unleash a second Godswar on Creation, putting far more lives in peril than he had hoped to save. [PARAGRAPH:2]His family urged him on, but they knew nothing of the hardships other nations had endured why Danalin protected their ancestors alone. His people had had their golden age, but Majosi knew that Man had been denied theirs by the act of pettier gods. He knew they deserved life more than he did. He said as much, but his apprentice would not listen. The boy grabbed the text and tried to pry the sacred spear from his webbed hands to finish the work, but Majosi hurled it into the depths where it remains unto this day. [PARAGRAPH:2]Trenton prayed that his god let them go that he might learn to care for Humanity as he had the Aifons, but the god was not ready to do so. Unable to personally intervene, Danalin unleashed all his beasts into Creation to guard his children, against he knew not what. Leviathan and the Great Scaled Dragon guarded the Isle from each side, awaiting the morning of the Aifon's predicted demise. [PARAGRAPH:2]No man nor god knows what happened on that morn. No Aifon soul reaches Danalin's vault, Arawn's Netherworld, or any heaven or hell. They simply vanished, or were consumed by something too horrible for words. Of the creatures sent to guard them, only Leviathan and the Scaled Dragon remained, but they were never the same. Driven mad by whatever they saw, these once wise and gentle beasts became the most vicious creatures in Creation. Leviathan was confined to the waves, but the dragon roamed far and wide, leveling cities in his wake. The Fire Rain did not slow him, nor did Mulcarn's entry into Erebus once the Illians found and completed Trenton's ritualn. Some claim that not even the new God of Erebus dared to face him, after seeing him devour the Aquilans he had sent to recruit the beast. [PARAGRAPH:2]His rampage could not last forever. In the twenty-third year since the deep freeze, the Beast met his match in Lucar and his horde. Legends tell of six thousand men of valor who saved the world from this abomination, in a sadly Pyrrhic victory. Lucar's spear struck true, but as the dragon breathed it last its heart burst open with not blood, but the greatest flood of brine ever seen in any land. The army arrayed against him was washed away in the deluge, which rushed down into the valley below, eroding twenty mountains, toppling the last of the Thraxian citadels, and drowning all who lived within. When the waters subsided all signs of civilization had been washed to floor bottom of the Aegean, a sea which is said to have tripled in size on that day. [PARAGRAPH:3]With the resurrection of Acheron, Drifa, and Abashi, rumors spread that this beast too may live again. Some Cultists claim that the Lords of the Aegean demand he be given new life, to drown all the realms of men and make all of Erebus submit to the Masters of the Depths. Mumbling Dreamers have begun to shout "Thalatth!" One Speaker of the Tide has proclaimed this to be the true name of the Crazed Dragon, but none can say for sure.

Adventurers are fearless and versatile heroes, which can upgrade to almost any type of unit. True to their name, they love looking for adventure rather than just doing the jobs they are assigned. Adventurers left in the wilderness may find lairs you never knew existed, and explore them without bothering to ask permission first. They will serve dutifully while fighting in hostile territory, but when left to guard the cities of their homeland they tend to get board and abandon their posts. Although it can be annoying at times, their short attention span can serve you greatly. They keep their old skills even after upgrading to something completely different, thus allowing possibilities like knights that can subdue beasts and summon elementals.

The Aquilan are the Seven Aspects of Mulcarn, powerful True Angels who take the form of great eagles that dwell in the heart of blizzards. Many assume that the aquilan seek out the blizzards, but in truth the blizzards are formed wherever the aquilan are.

Men-at-Arms are the upgrades of Axemen and Swordsmen. Their main role remains the same, primarily conquest of enemy cities. They can upgrade into any of three or four quite different units, so consider your goal when choosing promotions for them.
Colubra

Great Commanders can be used to either recruit units, build a Command Post in a city, or be added to another unit to increase its strength and the rate it gains experience points from combat. The recruit ability offers a quick random assortment of units, but the Command Post tends to have a better long term effect as it adds Great Commander points to the city making getting another all the more likely. A commander that is joined with a unit can always be split from the unit later on and used for other purposes, or joined to a different unit. Commanders may be used instead of Prophets to construct the holy shrines of The Order, The White Hand, and the Cult of the Dragon.
Counselor

The teachings of Sirona would never permit the Elohim to exalt or exploit Anger, Rage, and Hatred as the armies of most nations do; using Berserkers goes against everything the Elohim stand for. Instead, they employ Counselors who study anger only in order to help others understand the root causes of their suffering and overcome them. As disciples of Sirona they refuse to harm a living soul, but will defend those in their charge. When demons of anger and wrath roam Erebus, thousands remain sane only thanks to these Counselors.

The Elohim Berserker UU serves a very different purpose than most. These defensive-only units can make powerful defenders thanks to their Spirit [LINK=CONCEPT_AFFINITY]affinity[\\LINK], and have all levels of the spirit sphere promotions. They are most useful at calming units driven mad with the arrival of the Avatar of Wrath.

This special Undertow unit is created from the Drown spell. Whatever mortal is transformed into a Drown keeps its old base strength plus 2 Death Damage. Being undead, it is immune to death and poison damage. More importantly, Drowns gain the ability to move in coastal tiles as easily as on land, and can move through the Oceans too once the Theology tech is known.
Pixie

Pixies are the least combat oriented summon. They can defend but not attack. They are more useful to help your workers finish improvements or to sacrifice them in cities to hurry production, gain research, or add culture.

Pixies were created by Amathaon to tend to his gardens. Since Amathaon has retreated from creation they have been left behind and have spread out to any place that features beautiful flowers. Pixies have some magical powers but they mostly relate to simple illusions or the health of plants. They tend to distrust humans except for small children, who they sometimes protect or play with. One or two pixies sometimes abandon their gardens and move into more populated areas, preferring to live in the homes of artists or inventors. They are fascinated by new creations and are known to help with designs and projects when the artist is away or sleeping.

Eidola are demon disciple units that offer alternate upgrades for Champions and Priests. They require Iron or Mithril and an evil alignment, but no specific building. Priest upgraded to Eidola keep their spells, and melee upgraded to Eidola keep any melee-only promotions they have acquired, so consider upgrading rather than building directly. In any case, they're multi-use units with high strength and free march promotion.

The Illian Immortals have been given the same blessing and curse as the late Archangel of Ice, Taranis, in order to fill the role of the late archangel under the reign of the new God of Ice. Upon their ascension it becomes impossible to injure them, but equally impossible for them to grow, learn, or adapt to changing situations.

Iron Golems are likely to form the bulk of a Luchuirp army. They have high strength but as golems will not gain promotions from combat. They aren't going to end up as powerful as a highly promoted Man-at-Arms, but losing any one particular iron golem isn't likely to be a huge setback.

Lightbringers have all the abilities of ordinary [LINK=UNIT_DISCIPLE_EMPYREAN]Ecclesiastics[\\LINK] and more. Their [LINK=PROMOTION_PERFECT_SIGHT]Perfect Sight[\\LINK] lets them see invisible units. Like more advanced [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]Empyrean[\\LINK] units, they can help thwart rival spies. More importantly, they have no building requirement, a lower tech requirement, and double the chance to successfully spread the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN] the Empyrean[\\LINK]. This gives the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MALAKIM]Malakim[\\LINK] a significant head start in founding and popularizing that faith.
Sluagh

Sluagh are the souls of mortals who have died by not yet departed the world of Erebus. The gods send angels or demons to claim the spirits of their most devout followers, but most are left to wander the plane until they find passage to Arawn's realm. The draw of The Otherworld is strong, but can be resisted. A sluagh may long haunt an area if it feels a strong sense of duty to remain, but lingering too long is healthy for neither the spirit nor the world. These spirits often fall victim to evil necromancers, who raise them as undead monstrosities bound to follow the necromancer's will instead of its own. Only a few heroic souls have the strength of will to maintain their sanity, sense of identity, and the hope for a true resurrection. Resurrection spells cannot reach beyond the caster's own plane to restore any soul that has already entered its god's vaults. The Elohim obviate this restriction by assigning a soul catcher to their monarchs. A soul catcher is a mage specializing in spirit magic who can trap the soul after death and hold it until a resurrection is available. A god can answer prayers to send souls they have claimed back to Erebus for resurrection, but this is exceedingly rare. The only known examples are Duin Halfmorn and Arthendain, who were sent back by Camulos and Sucellus respectively.
Laroth

The Luonnotar are the most powerful disciple units to which the Grigori have access. Although they lack the spell abilities of priests and high priests, they are immune to magic, very strong in combat against other disciples, and can target disciple units in stacks with better defenders. They can move through rival territory without open border agreements, evangelizing the Children of The One religion to cities and units alike. Priests who adopt their faith are defrocked-- automatically disbanded. Other converts gain Scourge and Magis Resistance. In cities the faith can cause Monotheist revolts, forcing out other religions. Even state religions can be removed, plunging the city into chaos. The Grigori get a free Luonnotar when they first learn Arcane Lore, and can use it to found the Children of The One.

Radiant Guards have several advantages over axemen. They can see invisible, they start with the Guardsman promotion (allowing them to protect stacks from assassins and marksmen), and they can cast the Blinding Light spell to hold enemies in place. They can upgrade into Men-at-Arms or Rathas, which have all the strenghs of Chariots and more. They do not require Training Yards but do require both the Empyrean religion and a Fenestran Temple to be present in the city. They normally require the Empyrean state religion too, but the Overcouncil may pass a resolution allowing its members to ignore that restriction.

Rathas have several advantages over chariots. They can see invisible, they can cast the Blinding Light spell to hold enemies in place, and they have an a combat advantage against and the ability to target the sort of units which are enemies of Lugus. They may be trained only by those with the Empyrean as their state religion in cities where that faith and its temples are present.

Rathus Denmora has all the abilities of both [LINK=UNIT_GHOST]Ghosts[\\LINK] and [LINK=UNIT_DIVIDED_SOUL]Divided Souls[\\LINK], but his true value is as the ultimate counter other [LINK=PROMOTION_HERO]heroes[\\LINK]. He specifically targets heroes in stacks of stronger units (except in cities), and starts with the [LINK=EQUIPMENT_NETHER_BLADE]Nether Blade[\\LINK]. This otherworldly sword guarantees victory against heroes, and makes its victims ineligible for resurrection until the equipment is destroyed.

[TAB]How many roles have I played? They blur together in my mind. [PARAGRAPH:1]I was a victim from the moment my life began. An attacker came for my mother even as she gave birth to me. He possessed Garrus, a simple stable boy and used him to sneak up through the inn to my parents' room. He tried to get close to my mother, to attack her at her most vulnerable. My father fought to stop him. The details are unknown except that a battle occurred in the room and my father was struck a mortal blow. With his last breath he uttered a holy word that destroyed the spirit possessing Garrus and collapsed the entire inn. [PARAGRAPH:1]My mother died in the collapse, my father died from the attack. The stable boy was pulled from the rubble, one arm was crushed but he appeared otherwise healthy. My soul fled the dying infants form and took home in his newly evacuated body. I was born into the body of a teenage boy. [PARAGRAPH:1]The innkeeper raised me, teaching me as if I had simply forgotten my life and in a few years I served him well. He raised me as he rebuilt the inn. But I always knew that Garrus wasn't my name and I listened intently when those that survived the collapse retold the story. [PARAGRAPH:1]We didn't know much about my parents, but my father wore the yellow robes of a priest of the Empyrean. There was a small temple to the god in our city and when I was ready I joined their ranks as a disciple. Within the clergy my identity didn't matter, I was simply a child of Lugus. My superiors praised my empathy, questioned my maturity and laughed when I said that I thought I was the son of a priest. They claimed no such priest had visited the city and considered my thoughts the wishful thoughts of boy with too much imagination. [PARAGRAPH:1]My right arm was still crushed. By this point it was shriveled and permanently wrapped against my side. When I asked if it could be healed the priests prayed over it, but it never got better. Others came and received healing, nobles, merchants, beggars, soldiers, but I remained maimed. [PARAGRAPH:1]One day in early Aedrini the temple was in an uproar. Priests barked orders, disciples scurried about trying to look busy. No one had thought to wake me. After many questions a priest finally gave me my answer. [PARAGRAPH:1]"The Luminary Chalid is coming child, so stay out of the way. "[PARAGRAPH:1]I began to retreat to my chamber when he yelled after me, "And don't bother him when he arrives!"[PARAGRAPH:1]That next day a single man arrived on a dappled grey mare. He rode without an escort and though he needed no guards on the road, he could have used some outside of the temple. He was immediately mobbed by well meaning disciples, genuflecting priests and hordes of gawking townspeople. He wore the robes of a Luminary and I wondered if my father wore the same. [PARAGRAPH:1]He spent the next three days in our hastily constructed council chamber. The chamber was open for anyone to hear the deliberation and speak in an orderly manner. They discussed the towns role in the Overcouncil, local legislation and a problem with brigands in the area. [PARAGRAPH:1]The council meetings always went well into the night, and Chalid attended every dawn ceremony. He only had a few hours between to get some sleep. I was hurrying to the dawn service one morning when I found him standing alone in the refectory looking out the windows toward the east. The morning bell rung, signaling the dawn ceremony was about to start and Chalid turned to find me staring at him. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Morning disciple, are you ready to receive our lords blessing?"[PARAGRAPH:1]I managed to stammer something unintelligible out. Despite that he smiled at me with true affection and clasped me on the shoulder. That was the first he noticed my withered arm. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Do you have something to ask me?" he said. [PARAGRAPH:1]He expected me to ask for healing, but that didn't matter to me. Instead I asked, "What sort of spirit attacked my mother?"[PARAGRAPH:1]He put his arm around me and we walked to the sanctuary together. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Let me pray about it" he said. [PARAGRAPH:1]The service was exactly like all the others but I paid little attention. Instead I watched Chalid. He looked confused as he prayed, sometimes pained, sometimes resigned and I imagined that it had something to do with my question. [PARAGRAPH:1]I waited after the service. Chalid spoke briefly with the vicar who had performed the service and meet a few of the members. Then he left the sanctuary and went into the council chambers. [PARAGRAPH:1]I spent the day neglecting my duties and waiting outside the council chamber. Just past nightfall the towns warning bells rang out; guards ran through the streets yelling that brigands were attacking. [PARAGRAPH:1]Everyone flooded out of the temple. At the edge of the town shapes rushed through the darkness. Black tipped arrows cut guards down where they writhed screaming in pain. Guards brought torches and under the cover of shield men they retook the fortifications while the shadows simply moved to attack at another point. [PARAGRAPH:1]A voice from the darkness called, "What good is a god that abandons you every night?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Chalid ignored the taunt and ordered the men back within the cities lantern light. He alone bounded over the wall and in to the darkness at the cities edge. His mace glowed faintly in the starlight and though we couldn't see any attackers on the open field we all knew they were moving in on him. [PARAGRAPH:1]Chalid prayed and an aura of golden fire burst up around his head and dark men caught fire on the field, on the walls, and even a few that had snuck into the city. The holy fire consumed them and guards rushed in to beat or capture the men. [PARAGRAPH:1]But one was not distracted by the fire. It clung to his black armor and that of his steed but he rode soundlessly towards Chalid, like a shadow of a dark god stretching out to touch him. Chalid raised his mace up, and then back down and the field was lit up as if it was day. A pillar of golden fire, like the sun itself but full of righteous fury, crushed the rider. There was a horrific scream and then when the pillar retreated back up into the sky the rider was gone. [PARAGRAPH:1]I spent the night tending to the guardsmen wounded in the attack. Their wounds festered from poison and the men passed between fevered dreams and anguish when awake. There was little I could do but try to keep their wounds clean and try to make them comfortable. Chalid and the priests prayed over the men and some were healed, but too many were injured. [PARAGRAPH:1]That next morning I returned to my chambers to wash up and change into fresh clothes, as did most of the temple. I headed again to the dawn ceremony and found Chalid alone again in the refectory looking out towards the east. [PARAGRAPH:1]"You saved the town. " It sounded hollow when I said it. Unsuited to the miracle I had witnessed. [PARAGRAPH:1]"I only had faith that Lugus would protect me, he did everything else. "[PARAGRAPH:1]I smiled, the warmth Chalid had shared with me yesterday was gone now. He looked troubled but I assumed it was just the events of the long night. I know he hadn't slept either. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Did you find out anything about my mother?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Chalid looked at the floor, the morning bells rang though neither of us moved. [PARAGRAPH:1]"I should lie to you" Chalid said, "the mandate of truth is sometimes painful. I am sorry. I won't lie but I will warn you, it would be better if you did not know. "[PARAGRAPH:1]"I want to know" I argued with more passion than I intended, "Knowledge, truth, revelation are the precepts of Lugus. I should know my own past. "[PARAGRAPH:1]"The woman's name was Magda de'Vala" Chalid started, "The man wasn't her husband but her guardian, though he was a priest of the Empyrean. The child was prophesied to be a great hero, which is why many sought to kill Magda and her baby. "[PARAGRAPH:1]He paused, but I only waited for him to continue. [PARAGRAPH:1]"The stable boy Garrus died three days before the attack. That which killed Garrus, that which killed Magda's guardian and caused the collapse that killed Magda and her baby. that was you. "[PARAGRAPH:1]I was furious and I rushed out of the refectory. Chalid watched me go then headed into the sanctuary. My thoughts went back to those early days. I never felt like I was the stable boy. And for the first time I questioned my origin. Would a baby's spirit in a boy's body be able to adapt that quickly? Could even a possessed stable boy be able to overcome a priest of Lugus, or was that creature something darker? And was I that creature?[PARAGRAPH:1]I stopped in the temples infirmary. Except for the wounded it was empty, everyone in the temple was in the dawn ceremony despite those laying here near death. There was only one man awake, a bandage covered his left thigh. I knelt at his bedside. When I saw the torment he was in I forgot a bit of my own. [PARAGRAPH:1]"What is your name?" I asked. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Abin," he said, "I'm a jeweler who pretended to be a city guard. "[PARAGRAPH:1]That wasn't unusual. Our city was too small to maintain full time guardsmen so most were volunteers with other jobs. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Either you are too good at pretending, or not good enough. "[PARAGRAPH:1]He gave me a weak smile. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Can I pray for you?" I asked. He nodded. [PARAGRAPH:1]I placed my hand on him and closed my eyes. I have seen many healed but I had never performed a miracle myself. If I could do this, if I could heal this man and channel the power of Lugus then I couldn't be whatever creature Chalid thought I was. Maybe I was the holy child, maybe the attack on Magda de'Vala failed. [PARAGRAPH:1]I could feel his labored breath. I could feel his pain, feel his love for his large family of nieces and nephews. His quiet store and hours spent working on small intricate jewelry. And I felt him die. [PARAGRAPH:1]Then I felt the poison strike, it burnt through my body focused on the wound in my left thigh. I stepped away from the bed in shock. I was taller and my robes, which were big on me, were now tight. And my formerly withered arm was now trapped uncomfortably in its folds. [PARAGRAPH:1]I loosened the robe and held out my full, strong arm. But it didn't look like my arm; it was the jewelers arm. As I looked at myself I realized that I was identical to the dead body of the jeweler that lay in the bed in front of me. And then the poison struck again and sent me to my knees. I picked myself up and fled the temple in pain and confusion. [PARAGRAPH:1]Pain will drive you mad and it only took a few hours of suffering like this before I found a farmer out working in his field. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Blind goats Abin!" he said, "what is wrong with you? Why are you wearing a disciple's robes?"[PARAGRAPH:1]I threw him to the ground and held him, smashing him once in the face when he tried to fight back. I felt for that closeness, I reached out to find everything that he was, and the pain drifted away. When I opened my eyes I saw him staring up at his own reflection in horror. The last I saw him he was running toward his farmhouse, I started running as well. I don't think I have ever stopped. [NEWLINE][PARAGRAPH:1]I still don't know what I am. All the roles that I've played since then blur together in my mind. I've gotten better at reading people and worked for a time for an assassins' guild, simply for reading people I touch. During other times I steal the lives of those I wish to share. I tried the lavish extravagance of princes and wealthy merchants, but there is little to envy them for once you understand how they truly live. The best stolen lives come from the simple fathers of large families, those that have the love and respect of everyone in their lives. Dump the body of one of those in a shallow grave and I have a few good weeks of fun before I become bored and move on to something else. [PARAGRAPH:1]Maybe Chalid was right, maybe I am a monster.

The Empyrean is the youngest major faith in Erebus, having been organized only by its current Patriarch. The worship of the God of Light, however, is truly ancient. There were temples built in what would later become the Desert of Myrh which survived the worst of the Godswar, yet none survived the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH:1]Lanthus was a young Acolyte of Lugus from a time before the kingdoms of Man were first united. He was a righteous boy who lived a peaceful life of service to his community, until the day he met Alexis. In her quest to find immortality, she committed acts against him more egregious than any yet committed by mortal against mortal. She tortured him past the point that a living soul could bare, but would not let him die. When the finally had enough and decided to let is spirit leave his flesh, she devoured it and denied him the eternal rest that his god would have granted. Lugus is a forgiving lord, but even his forgiveness has bounds. He insists on actual repentance, on true contrition. Alexis could not find it in her heart to regret anything, but rejoiced in her inequity and proudly spread the secret of her dark arts to others just as cruel. Where all compassion had failed, Lugus considered it his duty to supplement the conscience, and so he cursed Alexis and her dark progeny. From that day forth, every beam of sunlight to touch a vampire's skin delivers with it a taste of all the suffering inflicted on others. While this causes no physical harm, it induces panic in minds unused to empathy and denies access to the superhuman powers stolen from the souls of others. [PARAGRAPH:1]Lugus always aims for the betterment of those he chastens, but the vampires refused to see his tough love through their own hate. They considered the curse a sign of a vendetta against them, and declared their own vendetta in return. Once Patria fell and could not constrain them, Alexis and Flauros led a campaign to eradicate every soul that honored the God of Truth. His church was destroyed. Every priest was executed. Every holy text was burned. Not one sentence of his doctrine was preserved intact. The Calabim made sure that the church of Lugus could not reemerge for over 600 years. [PARAGRAPH:2]It is however hard to crush the values of the human soul. The Malakim never abandoned their love of truth and openness. From time to time and in many tribes holy men would emerge and espouse such virtues. Lugus himself spoke into the hearts of many of these Lightbrigers. At the start of the Age of Rebirth, the name of Lugus was heard again. When the Once-Elf Varn Gosam wandered into the Desert of Myrh from the Vale of Shadows, he found a faith already emerging. He did not found the Empyrean by converting heathens, but by bringing together those who already loved The Light. Varn had united most of the Malakim in the worship of Lugus before he set out into the deep desert to find the legendary Mirror of Heaven, where Lugus reveled to him his holy doctrines in full.

These demons (also called "Drinkers") consume the souls of their victims, becoming more powerful each time they kill someone. After a few kills the Ira becomes so powerful opponents are better served to hide until they return to normal rather than try to kill it. [LINK=SPELL_ASSUAGE]Calming[\\LINK] spells are very effective against Ira, and weaken them considerably.

[TAB]The Luchuirp assaulted the Illian city. Juggernauts slammed against the defenses. Towering iron golems waded through the rubble, destroying any defenders they found. The Luchuirp forces tried to stop the ritual that was taking place within the inner city, but they were too late. [PARAGRAPH:1]When Mulcarn entered the city, entered creation, the battle stopped. A layer of ice spread from the first place his foot touched outwards through the city and across the land. The Luchuirp army was destroyed, dwarves killed, golems frozen. Even the Illian macemen were frozen in place, kept unchanged until Mulcarn needed them. [PARAGRAPH:1]As he surveyed his new dominion he picked up one of the Luchuirp golems. He admired their fortitude. They were unaffected by the cold and their unchanging nature. All traits Mulcarn prized. [PARAGRAPH:1]He whispered a new life into the golem, "Make me more. " [PARAGRAPH:1]"As you command" was Barnaxus's reply.

Illusionists have the abilities of normal mages, and also the abilities granted by the Illusionist promotion. Unlike in base FfH2, this does not make their summons illusions, but instead allows them to create illusionary duplicates of other units nearby. These illusions cannot attack much less kill opponents, but can be quite useful decoys to help defend your real troops.

Liches are Archmages who seek immortality through a sort of suicide. They use Necromancy to bind their own souls within their corpses, saving themselves from the horrors of hell, or any afterlife outside Erebus. The Lich's undead form is sustained through magic. Some use spells to preserve their flesh, some cast glamors to maintain the appearance of life, and some prefer to terrify their enemies by opening flaunting their corruption for all to see. Liches are always powerful casters and can be difficult to vanquish. They are naturally immortal, and restore their immortality with every kill. They are immune to all poisons and death damage, strong against unholy, but are vulnerable to holy damage, Undead Slaying, and the Destroy Undead spells. Each player is allowed only one Lich at a time. They must be upgraded from level 8+ units in a city with a Tower of Necromancy.

Valkyries were created to battle the demons who were stealing souls undeserving of hell. They escort the claimed to the heavens and attack demons attempting to stop the unclaimed from traveling to Arawn's realm.
The Ophanim are flying chariots manned by angels. They are swift and terrible. Though they fly their wheels still spin with the sound of crunching bones.

Heralds have the Herald's Call ability, which grants the Herald's Blessing promotion. This is both a blessing and a curse. It makes living units significantly more powerful, but then usually kills them within a few turns. They can return as Angels once they die, but it is still a good idea not to use this spell around units that are more useful alive than dead.

Angelic messengers often used to convey important messages. They convey not only words but usually powerful blessings, for example Nantosuelta may send a Herald to a general that grants valor and strength to his army. Priestesses of Ceridwen have been known to be able to capture and use the blessing of a Herald to their own ends
Maluka
Bael
Beedle
Gwenhwyfar the Swanmay

Bhall's Archangel Brigit can never be built, only [LINK=SPELL_FREE_BRIGIT]freed[\\LINK] from the [LINK=literal]Ring of Carcer[\\LINK] by a level 14+ unit once [LINK=literal]Fanaticism[\\LINK] is known. If Brigit acquires a [LINK=MASK_OF_ESUS]Mask of Esus[\\LINK], she may [LINK=SPELL_RETRIEVE_CORUNDUM_ARDENS]retrieve the Heart of Fire[\\LINK] and transform herself into [LINK=UNIT_SARABRIDE]Sarabride, Goddess of Vengeance[\\LINK], and found The Matronae.

Arawn's Archangel Gyra can never be built, only rescued from [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_BRADELINES_WELL]Bradeline's Well[\\LINK] or summoned using a Mercurian Gate and Death Affinity. If Gyra acquires a [LINK=MASK_OF_ESUS]Mask of Esus[\\LINK], she may [LINK=SPELL_RETRIEVE_OPALUM_MORTIS]retrieve the Ending Stone[\\LINK] and transform herself into [LINK=UNIT_MORRIGAN]Morrigan, Goddess of Fate[\\LINK], and found The Matronae.

Danalin's Archangel Condatis can never be built, only rescued from [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_AIFON_ISLE]Maenalus[\\LINK]. If Gyra acquires a [LINK=MASK_OF_ESUS]Mask of Esus[\\LINK], she may [LINK=SPELL_RETRIEVE_BERYLLUM_ABYSSI]retrieve the Ocean's Tear[\\LINK] and transform herself into [LINK=UNIT_CLIODNA]Cliodna, Goddess of Dreams[\\LINK], and found The Matronae.

Aeron's Archangel Odio can never be built, only [LINK=SPELL_FREE_ODIO]freed[\\LINK] from [LINK=literal]Odio's Prison[\\LINK] by a level 11+ unit once [LINK=literal]Rage[\\LINK] is known. Odio and the Ira whom he can summon are vulnerable to the [LINK=literal]Assuage[\\LINK] spell.

Ira are special units that may be summoned by the [LINK=UNIT_WRATH]Avatar of Wrath[\\LINK] or created in combat by [LINK=literal]Odio[\\LINK]. Although they start relatively weak, they go stronger whenever they kill an opponent. They are vulnerable to the [LINK=literal]Assuage[\\LINK] spell.

Chaos Marauders may appear in Sheaim cities with [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gates[\\LINK] and [LINK=BUILDING_CARNIVAL]Carnivals[\\LINK], and may be also summoned by the Chaos II spell. The summoned Marauders start out [LINK=literal]Rebellious[\\LINK], difficult to control and likely to betray you to the barbarian state. In either case the unit start out [LINK=literal]Mutated[\\LINK] and are vulnerable to the [LINK=SPELL_ASSUAGE]Assuage[\\LINK] spell.

Camulos originally created the Pacales as diplomats and traders. These angels were gifted with the ability to speak and understand any language as their original purpose was to smooth out relations between any intelligent species that may have conflict. That plan didn't last long. Shortly after the Angel of Peace fell to become the God of Strife, these peacemakers reversed their roles and became Chaos Marauders. These demons serve as mercenaries for hire, doing anything within their power to cause strife between various individuals, races, and empires. They still retain the ability to understand any language, but their speech jumps randomly between languages, making it nearly impossible for anyone but other marauders to understand more than small bits of what they are saying.

Abashi is among the greatest of Ceridwen's [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_OBSIDIAN]Obsidian Serpents[\\LINK]. She is not randomly generated from a Wyrmhold lair like her sisters, but may be trained directly by a Sheaim player after the [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\\LINK] ritual is completed. Like all [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_OBSIDIAN]Obsidian Serpents[\\LINK], her [LINK=SPELL_BREATH_NEXUS]breath weapon[\\LINK] is a bean of purple light that most think merely kills its victims, but may actually teleport them to a random location. Her roar transforms [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC]Dragon Fanatics[\\LINK] to [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC_OBSIDIAN]Obsidian Serpent Fanatics[\\LINK], as does that of her kin, but unlike them she cannot be compelled to attack a Fanatic's enemies via their [LINK=SPELL_BESEECH_DRAGON]Beseech Dragon[\\LINK] ability.

Acheron the Flame Lord is a rebellious creature, not even loyal to his Goddess Bhall much less to mortals who might temporarily subdue him. He is summoned into Erebus by the rage of the barbarians, long before the other dragons awaken. His entry into the world founds the Cult of the Dragon. Most players can only use [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\\LINK]to awaken other dragons if they have a city with the religion already present.

[PARAGRAPH:1]Drifa the Winter Wyrm [LINK=SPELL_BREATH_FROST]Breathes Frost[\\LINK], which does not summon any unit but can kill entire stacks directly. She was loyal to Mulcarn, but is not easily convinced that this means she should be loyal to Auric Ulvin. She will not serve him before he completes The Draw.

Eurabatres the Gold Dragon was the first of the dragons. Amathaon gave him gift to speak and understand all languages, including being able to speak to plants and animals, the wind, fire, earth and sea. The God of Creation largely stayed out of the Godswar, especially after the fall of the Fathers of Worlds, but Eurabatres continued to lead his armies against the forces of Agares. [PARAGRAPH:1]Since he merged his mind with Cardith Lorda in order to help him find a way to restore his true form, he has become an avatar of said leader. So long as Cardith is alive, he will switch to his control. The death of Eurabatres will cost Cardith his traits, but he can regain them by resurrecting the beast again.

The Scaled Dragons largely stayed out of the Godswar and were only used to protect the Aifons. Most were locked away at the signing of the Compact, but Thalatth was awakened to protect Maenalus again when in the Age of Magic it seemed Danalin's favorite people were in trouble. He was a gentle beast before, but witnessing whatever horror that destroyed the Aifons has driven him insane and hard to control. You can train him in Cult of the Dragon cities under the Undertow state religion, but doing so will drive your Scaled Dragon fanatics crazy too.

[TAB]Orthus, the self styled King of the Barbarians Hordes, is the most brutal and dangerous of the Orcish warlords. It is rumored that he was once a Bannor nobleman and close friend to King Khorde NuValle of Old Braduk before the Fall of Bhall, but there is no nobility or humanity left in this monster today. Even the Clan of Embers is far too civilized for him. He despises even their crude attempts at culture and scorns their loyalty to a goddess he considers as good as dead. While they revere their Bhall-Orcs, he would rather exterminate the whole priestly line. He already murdered the entire family of the last high priestess (except for one small orphan boy named Rantine, who managed to escape and devoted his life to opposing Orthus) in his quest to acquire the Matron Essendi. He then defiled this most sacred scepter by hafting it to a crude battle axe, which became a legendary weapon that fills its user with enough passion to fight on long past the point of exhaustion. [PARAGRAPH:1]Despite his barbarism, Orthus remains both very Charismatic and very Cunning. When he is created the Barbarian leader gains the Charismatic, Ingenuity, and Arrogating traits, which are then lost when he is killed.

[TAB]I was born to end an age of destruction. Dragons, angels, Leviathans, the mighty armies of the gods clashed as they struggled for advantage. Below, the earth trembled, and man was locked into a terrifying existence he could not hope to comprehend. [PARAGRAPH:1]The gods agreed on but one thing--that should they continue their struggle in the same vein or all their work would be lost. The spoils of their war, those sentient beings born of their cooperation at the time of creation, would be destroyed if an agreement was not made. [PARAGRAPH:1]So they came, one by one, to a distant corner of Erebus, until all 21 were assembled. The agreement was made, spelled out to the letter. I was the manifest symbol of that covenant, and its enforcement. The Godslayer. [PARAGRAPH:1]The oath each god made in turn bound their fate to me. As they spoke their agreement, their name became etched onto my surface. Then they left, never to set foot personally in creation again, on pain of death. I was left in the care of a human warrior. Centuries past. My purpose was forgotten--the Godslayer was used in battles and wars as any other blade. My pieces were split apart from use and time, but my nature cannot be destroyed. [PARAGRAPH:1]Mulcarn breaks his vow. Take me to him, for he has forfeit his life, and is sentenced to die upon my blade. Take me to him.
Kirien of Brigdarrow
Lyrr, Son of Adulin

The Crusader are an excellent counter for your opponent's Demonic units. Not only do they get a strength bonus against demons, but they are immune to disease, making them perfect to send into an area to eliminate any diseases The Ashen Veil and their Diseased Corpses have spread. [PARAGRAPH]There is a chance that a Crusader will automatically spread his religion to any city he conquers. The spread of The Order can cause more Crusaders to join your cause, and can also purge The Ashen Veil and The Undertow from the city.

Manes have a chance of being automatically created when an evil* unit dies or a neutral or evil city** is razed. They are gifted to [LINK=CIVILIZATION_INFERNAL]Infernal[\\LINK] civilizations and may be upgraded to most units. More importantly, they can also be [LINK=SPELL_ADD_TO_CITY]sacrificed to add population to a city[\\LINK]. Doing this transforms their experience into [ICON_CULTURE] and [ICON_PRODUCTION] for the city, and spreads their religion to said city. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]*Evil units include those with the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]Ashen Veil[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]Council of Esus[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\\LINK], or [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]White Hand[\\LINK] *** religion, those which practice [LINK=PROMOTION_DEATH1]Undeath[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_DIMENSIONAL1]Dimensional[\\LINK], or [LINK=PROMOTION_ENTROPY1]Entropy[\\LINK] magic, those with the [LINK=PROMOTION_VAMPIRE]Vampire[\\LINK] or [LINK=PROMOTION_UNHOLY_TAINT]Unholy Taint[\\LINK] promotion and those which are [LINK=PROMOTION_POSSESSED]Demon possessed[\\LINK]. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]**Whether razing a city generates Manes depends on both the alignment of its owner and on the alignment of the religions worshiped there. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]***Note that after [LINK=UNIT_AURIC]Auric Ulvin[\\LINK] [LINK=PROJECT_ASCENSION]Ascends[\\LINK], units and city population of The White Hand religion will return as Manes under the control of the new [LINK=UNIT_AURIC_ASCENDED]God of Winter[\\LINK] rather than being gifted to the Infernals.

Angels may be awarded to the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MERCURIANS]Mercurians[\\LINK] whenever good people die. This could be from a "good"* unit being killed, in which case they are made into an angel and maintain their experience to spend on new skills, or when a "good" city** is razed. Angels are the only units that can be upgraded into the Mercurians' most powerful units, so a healthy supply is crucial to their conquest of Erebus. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]*Good units are those who follow the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ORDER]Order[\\LINK], the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]Empyrean[\\LINK], or the [LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]Runes of Kilmorph[\\LINK] religion, have the Herald's Blessing promotion, or are controlled by Basium's team. It excludes animals and beast units. Note that things that make a unit qualify as evil take precedence over those that make it good; Empyrean units using death magic or Mercurian units of the [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]Council of Esus[\\LINK] religion would return as [LINK=CIVILIZATION_INFERNAL]Infernal[\\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_MANES]Manes[\\LINK] rather than Mercurian Angels. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]**Whether razing a city generates Angels depends on both the alignment of its owner and on the alignment of the religions worshiped there.

[ICON_BULLET]Angels of Death are excellent countermeasures to the [LINK=PROMOTION_UNDEAD]Undead[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_IMMORTAL]Immortals[\\LINK], and [LINK=PROMOTION_VAMPIRE]Vampires[\\LINK]. [NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET]The moral sort of [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_DEATH_ARAWN]Death Affinity[\\LINK] lets them cast [LINK=SPELL_DESTROY_UNDEAD]Destroy Undead[\\LINK] and [LINK=SPELL_HALLOW_GRAVEYARD]Hallow Graves[\\LINK]. [NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET]They defend first against various Undead, and can target immortals when attacking. [NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET]Their touch removes Immortality from any Living or Undead units that has found a way to cheat Arawn (or Laroth) of his due. [NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET]Cities they attack have their populations reduced. [NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET]Each source of [LINK=BONUS_MANA_DEATH]Death Mana[\\LINK] their plot's owner controls grants them a free promotion pick. [NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET]Angels of Death are [LINK=PROMOTION_INVISIBLE]Invisible[\\LINK] and capable of investigating rival cities.

One may not escape the angel of death, nor say to him, 'Wait until I put my affairs in order,' or 'There is my son, my slave: take him in my stead. ' Where the angel of death appears there is no remedy. [PARAGRAPH:0]These 'Angels of Death' are the Dullahan, mere servants of The Angel of Death, Arawn. He is a benevolent god, although always very dour. When The One gave The Twenty-One the power of creation, he commanded them that all their works were to be temporary, for they were not capable of making creatures perfect enough to endure the burden of true immortality. While Mankind condemns Agares as the creator of Evil, if was Nemed who first convinced his brethren to sin. Beholden to the precept of Life, he was willing to sacrifice his godhood to become the first man but unwilling to surrender his immortality. He convinced his brethren to create his wife Gabella as the crowning glory of Creation, a powerful and truly immortal woman who would bear him an immortal progeny. Arawn disliked this plan and cautioned against defying The One's wishes, but eventually agreed to abide by the majority decision. This proved disastrous. [PARAGRAPH]Once it was clear that Os-Gabella would bear no sons, the gods created Anesidora to take her place. This time the gods agreed to make humanity mortal, but they still insisted on granting us immortal souls. Arawn (who by then embodied the Precept of Life as well as Death) volunteered to tend to these disembodied spirits, granting them refuse and rest in his vault. He chose to let them choose their own fates, fashioning their own worlds within his just as the subconscious minds generates dreams. Arawn neither rewards nor punishes, but gives each soul what he believes he deserves. [PARAGRAPH]At first mankind recognized the gift of death as a welcome mortality from the weariness of life. In those early days, death was rare and experienced only by those who had lived a full life. The horrors of the Godswar and of the sorcery of the Age of Magic changed this greatly. The evil gods did much to make death more common, and more feared. Men terrified of the next world committed atrocities in order to bind their souls to this one. By the time of The Compact the gods had learned that souls were a valuable commodity, which they could use to create armies of angels and demons in order to increase their own power. Arawn alone abstained from this. He continued to take in more souls than any other god, but refused to exploit them for his own purposes. [PARAGRAPH]Arawn abhors the perversions of Undeath. It was for this reason that he create The Dullahan. During the Age of Magic he would send out these True Angels to gather souls and guide them to their resting place, lest they be stolen by other gods or bound to their own decaying flesh. [PARAGRAPH]Once he surrendered the Precept of Life to Sucellus, the God of Death withdrew further into himself. He now refuses to have anything to do with Erebus, and will scarcely acknowledge that it exists. The armies of the Dullahan still long to fulfill their purpose, but cannot do so in his service. While many still follow Gyra, the Archangel of their sphere, many others have abandoned their god in order to serve in the armies of her twin. Others have taken an even darker path and are determined to help Laroth destroy Arawn so that they can follow a god who will lead the dead to conquer the lands of the living. [PARAGRAPH:3]Faeryl Viconia and Barbatos plot to summon Gyra, the Archangel of Death. Faeryl plans to command Gyra to kill Arendel, the queen of the Summer Court, and Barbatos wants Gyra to remove the curse Arawn has placed upon him and end his own life. [PARAGRAPH]Though their ritual is exhaustive and requires sacrifice from both of them, it does not summon or bind Gyra herself. Instead one of the Dullahan, servants of the Norns, is trapped by their spell. His name is Dumah and he is the spirit of silence and the stillness of death. [PARAGRAPH]The Dullahan are charged with ending immortal life, but even they can't end Arawn's curse on Barbatos. Faeryl still turns the Dullahan against Arendel. The Dullahan slips into the Summer Court capital on the Winter Solstice, when the city is usually quiet. He walks unhindered through the city, guards unknowingly deciding to check other posts, and the few citizens on the street unknowingly taking other routes as their instincts guide them to avoid Dumah's path. [PARAGRAPH]Dumah sits for a season in the throne room of Arendel, and though he stands in the room no one notices him. They look away as he watches the beautiful queen rule her kingdom with honor and passion. He sees her cry for her empire's losses when she thinks the throne room is empty, and feels the weight of ages of hard decisions upon her. He also witnesses her fierce strength and resolve in leading her people. [PARAGRAPH]Knowing her guards will sacrifice themselves to protect her, that he will kill those guards, and the weight of those useless deaths on Arendel, Dumah waits until the palace is quiet and the queen is alone. Then he casts back his cloak and appears to her as an angel of death, radiating with ancient power, immutable and eternal. [PARAGRAPH]Dumah calls to Arendel, telling her of the great love he has for her, but commanding that her time is ended; this eternal life is not meant for mortals. She cannot escape death. [PARAGRAPH]Arendel's ring summons her personal guard to her. Devon, an elven warrior and direct son of Nemed, attacks the Dullahan. Though Devon is strong and blessed with holy power, he does not injure the Dullahan. Instead the Dullahan strikes Devon, leaving him broken and dying on the throne room floor. [PARAGRAPH]Arendel pleads with Dumah. She offers to give up her immortality, to let death come for her as it will, but not on this night. The Dullahan should retreat and return for her when death comes naturally for her. Dumah agrees. [PARAGRAPH]Arendel restores Devon by passing him the Phoenix with which Sucellus had blessed her. This provides the Son of Nemed with the health, strength, and eternal youth she had enjoyed for ages. Arendel gives him the ring that she used to summon him, releasing him from her charge. He has given his life for her once; she can ask no more from him. [PARAGRAPH]Dumah retreats, staying hidden but always close to the summer queen, watching her finally begin to age as the seasons pass, and waiting for the moment they will meet again.

A wyvern is a large flying serpent with a tail ending in a scorpion's stinger. They are rare in the Age of Rebirth, having been hunted almost to extinction by knights responding to reports of them stealing livestock or threatening rural families. They were much more common during the wars of the Age of Magic, when the students of Kezef and Leucetios created them as a poor imitation of true dragons.
Wyvern Rider
Wyverns are powerful winged serpents created by human archmages in the Age of Magic. Few survive in the Age of Rebirth.

Gibbon Goetia is a [LINK=PROMOTION_CHANGELING]changeling[\\LINK] who can takes the form and abilities of those he kills. (Due to potential complications in the code, this ability does not work on animals, beasts, or those units that will abandon players who do not maintain the right civic or state religion. ) If you use his to target stronger opponents, he will himself become stronger. Should the form he assumes seem inferior to his natural state, you may use his [LINK=SPELL_ASSUME_TRUE_FORM]Assume True Form[\\LINK] ability to get rid of the disadvantage.

All vampires have unnaturally long life-spans, stolen from their victims, but the vampire lords have learned to cheat death itself. Whether through massive feasting or some more arcane ritual, the body of a vampire lord is recreated upon destruction. Some spend their stolen years further honing their martial prowess, but many, having experienced everything else in life, study forbidden knowledge, learning to cast the most advanced Body, Death, Mind, and Shadow spells. A few take the final step towards immortality, and become a Lich.

Colubrae have a chance of appearing in Sheaim cities with a [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gate[\\LINK] and an [LINK=BUILDING_OBSIDIAN_GATE]Obsidian Gate[\\LINK] building. The units start out [LINK=literal]Mutated[\\LINK] and can learn mage level spells.

Colubrae are snake-men with the lower bodies of snakes, snake heads and humanoid arms. There is a wide variety within their species, some are poisonous, some exceptionally large or strong, other have two heads or a variety of other mutations. They can be powerful warriors and spell casters, which is unusual outside of those descended from Nemed (humans and the derived races). It isn''t known if this talent is due to some human ancestry or the influence of Ceridwen. Colubra often work as mercenaries for less ethical warlords, and tend to inhabit remote locations sacred to Ceridwen, which usually means the site has its own unusual properties. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Mobius Witches are priestesses of [LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Between[\\LINK], and have a chance of appearing in Sheaim cities with a [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gate[\\LINK] and [LINK=BUILDING_MAGE_GUILD]Mage Guild[\\LINK] buildings. They share the abilities of [LINK=UNI_MAGE]Mages[\\LINK], except they cannot gain affinities based on your mana supply or [LINK=PROMOTION_MASTERY]The Tower of Mastery[\\LINK] as they are disciples rather than arcane units. They can use both [LINK=SPELL_SEVER]Astral Projection[\\LINK] and the para-drop mechanic to travel several tiles away without passing through intervening tiles.

Once human, the mobius witches live in the bizarre between worlds of Ceridwen. In Erebus they have an odd fascination with edges, corners and doorways, sometimes to the point of fearing them. Though they display little interest in relationships with humans or with each other they are as insightful to the nature of relationships as they are obtuse about the physical world. Mobius Witches are powerful spell casters, occasionally using magic unfamiliar to Erebus (rune magic originally came from them). -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Revelers are automatically created in Sheaim cities that contain a [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gate[\\LINK] and a [LINK=BUILDING_GAMBLING_HOUSE]Gambling House[\\LINK]. They are very useful as scouts as they can see very well, despite the caecus cloth that cover their eyes, even detecting invisible units around them.

Manticores have a chance of appearing in Sheaim cities with a [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gate[\\LINK] and a [LINK=BUILDING_TEMPLE_UNBLEMISHED]Garden[\\LINK]. These beasts are powerful attackers who can fly and heal themselves by consuming their living victims.

Lions with wings and tails that can fire iron spikes larger than a crossbow bolt. A full grown manticore stands nearly seven feet at the shoulder. Manticores have a voracious appetite and there are few who can afford to feed them when they are kept as guards. Likewise they are likely to overhunt their area when living in the wild and are unable to settle in one area. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Succubi are [LINK=PROMOTION_DEMON]Demons[\\LINK] who can [LINK=PROMOTION_WINGED]fly[\\LINK] and [LINK=SPELL_CHARM_PERSON]charm[\\LINK] their victims. They can be [LINK=SPELL_RECRUIT_MERCENARY_SUCCUBUS]recruited[\\LINK] as [LINK=PROMOTION_MERCENARY]mercenaries[\\LINK] by worshipers of the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]Ashen Veil[\\LINK], but more commonly appear in Sheaim cities with the [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gate[\\LINK] and [LINK=BUILDING_PUBLIC_BATH]Public Baths[\\LINK] buildings. They may also be summoned by units with a [LINK=PROMOTION_PACT_WITH_SALLOS]Pact[\\LINK] with [LINK=LEADER_SALLOS]Duke Sallos[\\LINK].

Succubi are powerful seducers. They can appear as female or male (in which care they are called Incubi) but their gender makes little difference to them. They were created to tempt mortals or occasionally sire cambions with them. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Tar Demons have a chance of appearing in Sheaim cities with a [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gate[\\LINK] and [LINK=BUILDING_TEMPLE_OF_THE_VEIL]Temple of the Veil[\\LINK] buildings. These lazy denizens of Mulcarn's hell are heavy and can use the [LINK=SPELL_SLOW]Slow[\\LINK] spell. When killed, large enough tar demons will split into two smaller tar demons.

Hollow men are the ghosts of those who served Mulcarn in the Age of Ice. They are most common around Letum Frigus and typically appear and thin, pale, indefinite creatures that are nearly invisible in a snowstorm. They rarely attack formidable opponents, preferring to find those freezing in the wastes and steal the last bits of warmth from their bodies. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Wind Knight
The Pegasus is a sacred symbol of Tali, and the preferred mount his worshipers. These beasts can never truly be tamed, but they have been known to form friendships with knights of the Foxmen.
This Foxman religious champion is the most mobile unit available to most players. It is extremely fast and can fly across continents.
Unseelie Shadow

An unaligned Dragon Fanatic may spread the Cult of the Dragon, is a scourge to the clerics of the gods, and has the courage to approach a dragon or dragon lair in order to devote himself to the beast's service. It may betray you to serve the first dragon it finds, and in the process upgrade to a more powerful dragon fanatic devoted to that specific dragon species. A Fanatic of a particular dragon will always abandon you if given the chance to serve that kind of dragon instead, unless you too have that kind of dragon.

Wyvern Riders among the fastest and most powerful mounted units, capable of flying across oceans and continents almost as fast as the Foxmen's Wind Knights. They cannot be trained directly must be upgraded from a Wyvern, much like a War Elephant is upgraded from a normal Elephant.

The sons of fire are powerful attackers. These fire-immune angels do collateral damage to stacks they attack and can cast the [LINK=SPELL_PILLAR_OF_FIRE_BRIGIT]Pillar of Fire[\\LINK] spell to devastate stacks without attacking. They are a terror to enemy units and can decimate entire armies.

The Seraphim appear as angels surrounded in a halo of golden fire. They are commonly used as seekers, used to retrieve those who have violated divine law and bring them back for judgment. Many of the Seraphim are angels who used to be under Bhall and refused to fall with her. Most of the gods are suspicious of the Seraphim, and several have fallen even since Bhall''s fall to become powerful fallen angels, but Lugus remains loyal and welcoming to the Seraphim that serve him. A Seraph feather is thought to be a powerful token of love and devotion. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Of the beasts formed by men only the centaurs retain some part of their noble nature. Many creatures were made from the bodies of men, but they were often reduced to the passions of their bestial form. Perhaps it is because the animal they were made from, the majestic stallions of the Cerici, were known for their docile nature as well as their strength. But do not assume that the Centaurs are passive. Those creeping into their glades expecting gentle pacifists bounding away like deer when they see strangers will be surprised by the firm, battle-hardened giants they find. Centaurs are fond of war paint and other body art, thick, dangerous weapons, and feasts of wild fruit and meat so undercooked it drips with blood. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

These beasts have sworn their loyalty to Hastur, the lord of nightmares and archangel of Mammon. They dwell in the deepest oceans and rarely come to the surface except at the bidding of dark priests. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Krakens are powerful beasts that dwell beneath the waves (especially around [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_AIFON_ISLE]The Maenalus[\\LINK]) and make the seas perilous to all who oppose [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\\LINK]. As servants of Hastur they have [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_MIND]Mind Affinity[\\LINK] letting them [LINK=SPELL_CHARM_PERSON]Charm[\\LINK] weaker minds. They spend most of their time [LINK=SPELL_SUBMERGE]submerged[\\LINK] and thus [LINK=PROMOTION_HIDDEN]invisible[\\LINK] to most units except just after an attack, but can still blockade ports to make maritime trade impossible. Barbarian Krakens submerging in the territorial waters of players with [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\\LINK] as their State Religion may choose to serve those players for a time, as may those who are disturbed by a [LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_OF_THE_OVERLORDS]Cultist's[\\LINK] [LINK=SPELL_TSUNAMI]Tsunami[\\LINK], but they are notoriously disloyal unless summoned by [LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_OF_THE_OVERLORDS]Speaker of the Tide[\\LINK]

The nive are large beasts covered in thick grey fur. They are typically so covered in snow that they are almost impossible to distinguish from the terrain, especially in snowstorms. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Ogres are huge, averaging about nine feet and occasionally as large as twelve feet tall. They are unusual in that their coloration varies dramatically between individual ogres covering every end of the spectrum. Some are hairless and some are completely covered in a thick coat of fur. They are among the races descended from the fallen Bannor, men devoted to Bhall who were transformed into raging beasts by her fall. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Sometimes called "the Grey" or "the Breathless," Shades are men that gain immortality by slowly spending their souls in a ritual developed by Laroth and snuck out of the underworld by the "Once-Elves. " Over centuries shades lose their passion, and though they continue to live they become passionless shadows of their former selves. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Dark riders and the elite of Esus's humanoid units. When deception has finally reached its limit Esus turns to the shadowriders. The shadowrider's most powerful ability is to ignore physical material, allowing them to charge right through walls or shieldmen to get at other targets. Conversely bright light acts as a physical barrier for them and they are unable to enter a brightly lit area, extremely slow in sunlight, and a focused beam of light will cut through them. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Shadowriders are national units that must be built or upgraded in a city with the [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]Council of Esus[\\LINK] religion present, by players with the [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]Council of Esus[\\LINK] state religion, and will abandon players who abandon that faith. They are among the most powerful units in the game, having a decent base combat, plus poison damage, plus [LINK=CONCEPT_AFFINITY]affinity[\\LINK] for [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SHADOW]Shadow Mana[\\LINK] which means their total strength is limited only by how many sources of the resource you can secure. They are highly mobile, more so even than ordinary knights due to their ability to ignore all terrain costs and even impassible terrains. They also ignore city defenses, first strikes, and defensive strikes, making them excellent at conquering enemy strongholds. Like assassins, they can choose to target either the strongest or weakest defenders of a stack. They are easily the strongest unit that begins with [LINK=PROMOTION_HIDDEN_NATIONALITY]Hidden Nationality[\\LINK], and can regain that promotion at will through casting [LINK=SPELL_MASK]Mask[\\LINK]. Their [LINK=PROMOTION_STEALTH]Stealth[\\LINK] also lets them [LINK=SPELL_HIDE]become[\\LINK] [LINK=PROMOTION_HIDDEN]Hidden[\\LINK]. The only real weakness of these elite cavalry is the power of Lugus the Light, and the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]Empyrean[\\LINK] units that worship him.

Duin Halfmorn was one of the greatest of Camulos's worshipers. He came from humble beginnings and survived as a serial killer and cannibal before taking control of a small bandit ring to extend his brutality. Eventually the bandits became outraged by his behavior, though their attempt to overthrow him failed and he feasted on their hearts. He prayed to Camulos for more loyal followers and Camulos blessed him with the ability to infect others with lycanthropy, changing victims into ravenous werewolves. Though this didn't result in very loyal followers for Duin, he enjoyed being able to spread his curse and has produced generations of werewolves since. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Pit Beasts are tormented souls trapped in the chasm prisons of Camulos's hell. They are strong and mindless outside of basic animalistic urges. They have become so acclimated by pain that not only do they not fear it, but they are driven by a desire to feel it and inflict it on others. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Souls bound into the skeletal remains of a creature. Most of the time it's a human but they can also be animals or magical beasts. Skeletons have few thoughts beyond wanting to end life and they will attack anyone they come into contact with. Necromancers have to use magic to give them an aura of the undead to keep their skeletons from attacking them. Occasionally a skeleton will become obsessed with some fragment of his former life. A skeleton may carry a teddy bear, guard the ruins of a house, or wander behind a flock of sheep. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Sometimes when someone so corrupt and vile dies the ground will not accept them. Heaven and even the afterworld are closed to them, it should be demons that bear their souls to hell. But occasionally the demons will leave them in creation. Bitter and dark these souls turn into spectres. Eventually demons will come for them, but until then the soul has more time to haunt the world. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Elementals are spirits from the elemental vaults bound into a physical form on Erebus. They are not alive. There are as many types as there are inorganic materials to inhabit. Commonly these tend toward fire, earth, air and water elements but they can inhabit sand, smoke, sunlight, darkness, gold, lightning, lava, and a variety of other forms. The strength of the elemental is determined by that of the spirit that was summoned and the purity of the element he was summoned into. For example, one mage had the habit of summoning earth elementals from graveyards, and though horrifying to have the corpses and coffins of the dead as part of the elemental's body it weakened the elemental. -- The Bestiary of Erebus
